Medicine connects the mechanisms of health and disease with clinical reasoning, physical examination, patient contact, research and medical professional development. This comparison follows the regular 2024 entrant cohort through its three documented years.

This UCR programme provides sustained scientific study of human health and disease, with anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, infection, neuroscience and health research. These subjects respond directly to Medicine’s scientific foundations. Clinical reasoning levels, physical examination, acute medical skills, assessed patient care and medical professional formation remain substantial gaps; psychology and biomedical laboratory courses do not replace them.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Regular Medicine, 2024 entrant cohort

The documented cohort comprises 60,56 and64 EC across its three years. Clinical and research minor topics depend on the permitted selection. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC. RADAr participation is an additional 0-EC requirement; passing it is not required.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Medicine at Radboud University with 1 illustrative UCR study composition.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Human health, disease and behaviour

Study the scientific basis of human health and disease through anatomy, physiology, molecular pathology, pharmacology, infection, neuroscience, psychology and health research. This is a sustained medical-science response to Medicine’s disease-mechanism and evidence strands. It does not provide the programme’s clinical reasoning and examination sequence, assessed patient care, acute medical skills or physician qualification.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Ethics
Ethics examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, alongside moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Students apply ethical arguments to issues including equality, poverty and wealth, animal rights, future generations, climate change and historical injustice. Papers and presentations develop independent argumentation.
Close

Epidemiology & Public Health
Introduces epidemiology and the evidence used in public health. It examines disease patterns, risks and changes over time, and how research can inform decisions about population health.
Close

Functional Anatomy
Studies human anatomical structure in relation to function through surface anatomy, medical imaging, scientific drawing, dissection-related materials and clinical demonstrations. These are academic learning activities rather than clinical skills training.
Close

Pharmacology
Covers the science of drugs—their origin, composition, kinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity. Discusses drug targets, interactions and kinetics, enabling students to explain therapies in terms of molecular targets and physiological consequences.
Close

Infection & Immunity
Explores fundamental processes in immunology such as recognition of self vs non‑self, lymphocyte receptor development and innate and adaptive immune responses. Examines host‑pathogen interactions, inflammation, tissue damage and immunopathology.
Close

Mechanisms of Disease
Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease. It connects embryology, anatomy and physiology with symptoms and failures in the cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, digestive, endocrine and central nervous systems.
Close

Neurobiology
Neurobiology studies the biological basis of behaviour through evolutionary pressures, biorhythms, comparative anatomy, animal models and selected disorders. Students examine research ethics and animal welfare, practise laboratory techniques such as microscopy and cell staining, and compare brain anatomy across species.
Close

Perception & Action
Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Close

Higher Order Functions
Higher Order Functions deepens knowledge of neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental cognitive neuroscience. Topics include memory, emotion, social cognition, attention, consciousness, decision-making and planning. Students evaluate current research and develop experimental designs.
Close

Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
Introduces cells, molecular biology, cellular physiology and communication. It connects genetic information and variation with living systems and offers initial perspectives on life sciences, biomedicine and public health. A research presentation develops engagement with scientific literature.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Molecular Cell Biology
Provides foundation for practical applications in life science. Focuses on cellular biology of eukaryotes and prokaryotes, revisits concepts from introductory courses, examines current research and encourages evaluating reproducibility and modernising methods.
Close

Human Physiology
Studies normal functioning of the human body, covering structure‑function relationships, energy handling, homeostasis, signalling, organ systems and integration of their functions.
Close

Biochemistry
Explores the chemistry of life and biomolecules such as proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids. Discusses metabolic pathways, the role of biomolecules in health and disease and applications in medicine, biotechnology and sustainability.
Close

Life Science Laboratory
Introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work. Covers themes like blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics and provides a foundation for clinical and biomedical research.
Close

Molecular Pathology & Genetics
Covers general and molecular pathology and genetics. Studies cell injury, death, inflammation, immunity, tissue repair, regeneration, fibrosis and neoplasia, examines genetic mutations and diseases, and discusses genetic testing and ethical considerations.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

Abnormal Psychology
Provides a deep dive into factors shaping mental health. Teaches critical thinking, explores the bio‑psycho‑social approach and covers mental disorders, research findings and assessment techniques.
Close

Medical & Health Psychology
Uses a biopsychosocial approach to explore how biological, psychological and socio‑cultural factors influence health and illness. Covers theories, research and interventions and focuses on the role of psychological expertise in medical settings.
Close

Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
Introduces concepts, methods and ethical issues in clinical psychological assessment and psychotherapy. Students compare approaches to assessment and treatment across age groups and learn to evaluate information critically.
Close

Advanced Research Seminar
Advanced Research Seminar introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.
Close

Lifespan Developmental Psychology
Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.
Close
